summary: The biggest fresh signal is Lilly's TRANSCEND-T2D-2 result. In adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, retatrutide was compared head-to-head with semaglutide 2 mg. At 80 weeks, A1C fell 2.2% on both retatrutide doses versus 1.8% on semaglutide. Weight fell 19.5% (9 mg) and 20.9% (12 mg) versus 9.4%. This is the efficacy estimand, from company topline data that is not yet peer-reviewed. Coverage is everywhere (Reuters, STAT, ABC, NY Post, BioSpace, Fox affiliates). But the result went public on Oct 28 at about 10:45 GMT, so the strict 48-hour Lane C window closes around 06:45 ET on Oct 30, before the 14:00 ET long-form slot. Default treatment: the 13:00 retatrutide Short ("new Phase 3 data", with a loop ending), plus the side-effect and dysesthesia angle as a body-worry Short later in the week. A Lane C long-form only goes ahead if the Editor-in-Chief accepts a roughly 55-hour gap. With no qualifying news, today's long-form defaults to Lane A, in playbook order: stopping tirzepatide (SURMOUNT-4), then protein, hair loss, bones and muscle, and plateau. Each one now has a fresh hook (CBC's on/off feature, the YouGov survey of what GLP-1 users eat, the Oct 28 Diabetes Obes Metab 12-month real-world study, and the Arch Osteoporos review). New, verified Short and Reel fuel: (1) a tirzepatide pancreas and gallbladder scoping review (11 RCTs; pancreatitis in 11 participants across 5 trials). (2) A Menopause Society 2026 retrospective study of about 3,900 women, where those also on hormone therapy lost about 11% versus 9.5% at 1 year on semaglutide, with a smaller difference on tirzepatide. It's preliminary and not peer-reviewed. (3) The syndicated Sinclair 'doctor warns of long-term side effects' story, which suits an honest-uncertainty format. Thanksgiving on tirzepatide is a seasonal evergreen and has now been seen in 3 snapshots. It should be built now to rank before the Nov 20–26 peak. Rejected: microdosing (Yahoo Health recirculated it Oct 29) and the 'cheapest compounded tirzepatide' press release. Endometrial cancer, cost and coverage, employer plans and the bariatric surgery angles were skipped as banned, underperforming or too uncertain.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide vs semaglutide 2 mg head-to-head in type 2 diabetes (TRANSCEND-T2D-2, Phase 3, 1,298 adults, 80 weeks): A1C −2.2% on both retatrutide doses vs −1.8%; weight −19.5% (9 mg) and −20.9% (12 mg) vs −9.4% (Lilly topline, Oct 28, 2026)
candidates.angle: 'What's confirmed?' with a loop ending. Retatrutide beat semaglutide 2 mg on blood sugar and weight in adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, with or without an SGLT2 inhibitor. Then the honest half: more people stopped because of side effects (4.8% on 9 mg and 7.9% on 12 mg, vs 2.7% on semaglutide). The open-label, efficacy-estimand and 'not yet peer-reviewed' caveats come next, then what happens next (more Phase 3 readouts due by end of 2026; full results at a future conference). Put retatrutide first in the title. State the population as type 2 diabetes, baseline BMI about 36.8. Not approved; never mention gray-market sources.

candidates.why_now: First Phase 3 head-to-head of retatrutide vs semaglutide, released Oct 28. Mainstream pickup is already heavy (Reuters, STAT, ABC, NY Post, Fox affiliates, Everyday Health), plus Medical Daily's 'more patients quit' angle on Oct 30. Retatrutide Shorts on new Phase 3 data are our proven peaks (268, 202). Timing: the 48-hour Lane C window closes about 06:45 ET Oct 30, so this defaults to the 13:00 Short. Long-form only if the Editor-in-Chief accepts about 55 hours.
